title: Introduce counterfactual anchor prober with confidence-decay soft-fail CI gate
author: Claire Nguyen
description: Motivation: Some prompt-set regressions are only exposed when small counterfactual perturbations interact with model calibration. This PR adds a counterfactual anchor prober and a companion confidence-decay soft-fail CI gate to detect subtle, distribution-sensitive regressions early. Design summary: 1) counterfactual_anchor_prober: Generates controlled counterfactual variants for each prompt anchor using lightweight perturbation operators (lexical swap, entity obfuscation, tense-shift) and computes an ensemble disagreement + calibration-adjusted robustness score per anchor. 2) confidence_decay_gate CI hook: Aggregates anchor scores across a prompt-set and applies a decaying confidence budget so transient outliers do not block merges but sustained decay triggers a soft-fail (annotated CI failure) and opens an automated investigation ticket. 3) Integrations: Wire prober output into the existing eval-report JSON schema, add telemetry for per-anchor failure modes, and add a remediation suggestions block that lists candidate prompt fixes or recommended model rollout throttles. Implementation notes: - New module eval_harness/probers/counterfactual_anchor.py implements generator and scoring pipeline with pluggable perturbation registry. - CI hook implemented at ci/hooks/confidence_decay_gate.py and registered in .github/workflows/eval-ci.yml as a post-eval step. - Small helper in eval_harness/utils/calibration.py adds confidence-adjusted scoring utilities used by other gates. - Tests: unit tests for perturbation operators and end-to-end smokecases in tests/probers/test_counterfactual_anchor.py. - Docs: docs/eval/counterfactual-anchor.md explains configuration knobs and migration notes. Testing and validation: ran the new prober across three canonical prompt-sets (chatbot-support, email-compose, code-generation) and used historical snapshots to verify that the gate triggers only for sustained degradations (simulated via injected perturbation noise). CI run initially failed due to a nondeterministic tokenization edge-case in one perturbation operator; fixed by normalizing whitespace in the generator and reran. Backwards compatibility and rollout: default configuration is disabled for global CI and enabled in an opt-in eval policy named "counterfactual-guard-v1". We will enable it on the nightlies for two weeks before lifting to PR gating. Security and perf: perturbations run in-process and are lightweight; added an execution timeout and caps on variant count to prevent runaway cost. Checklist: - [x] Prober implementation and unit tests - [x] CI hook + workflow registration - [x] Integration into eval-report schema - [x] Docs and migration notes - [x] Telemetry counters and tracing annotations - [x] Manual smoke runs and historical backtests Related work: builds on prior anchor/replay ideas (see ENG-1176) but focuses on counterfactual perturbations and calibration-driven confidence decay to reduce false-positive gating. Linear/Jira: ENG-1289 epic for regression-detection features, ENG-1292 task for CI gate integration, SUP-4421 customer incident that motivated counterfactual checks. Rollout plan: opt-in -> nightlies -> staged PR gating for 10% org -> full PR gating if noise < 2% over 14 days. Notes: the prober registry is intentionally extensible so other teams can add domain-specific perturbations (e.g., API param shuffling for developer-facing prompt-sets).
commits: feat(probers): add counterfactual_anchor_prober and perturbation registry
feat(ci): add confidence_decay_gate hook and register in eval CI workflow
chore(tests): add unit and e2e smoke tests for counterfactual prober
docs: add counterfactual-anchor usage guide and rollout notes
fix(tokenization): normalize whitespace in perturbation generator to prevent nondeterministic diffs
review_comments: Ravi Patel: Nice design. Two asks: (1) can we limit total variants per anchor by default to 20 and (2) add a short-circuit so high-confidence anchors skip heavy perturbations?
Author (Claire Nguyen): Implemented variant cap and short-circuit; updated docs to surface these knobs.
Marta Lopez: CI hook looks good, but pls add an allowlist for sensitive prompt-sets that should never have perturbations run in CI.
Author: Added allowlist support and a fallback opt-out via environment variable EVAL_ANCHOR_ALLOWLIST.
Evan Chen: Telemetry looks fine. One nit: use exponential decay with half-life config instead of linear decay to better match observed regression patterns.
Author: Switched to configurable exponential decay and added tests for decay behavior.
ci_summary: GitHub Actions eval-ci: initial run failed (test: test_perturbation_whitespace) -> tokenization nondeterminism; fix tokenization normalization -> rerun
Secondary checks: lint (pass), mypy (pass), integration-run (pass), perf-smoke (pass), nightly-backtest (pass)
release_notes: Introduce a pluggable counterfactual anchor prober and a confidence-decay soft-fail CI gate to detect sustained, subtle prompt-set regressions. Opt-in by default and can be enabled via eval policy 'counterfactual-guard-v1'. Adds telemetry, docs, and remediation suggestions.
risk_profile: low-medium: non-invasive opt-in feature; CI gate defaults to soft-fail and has caps/timeouts to limit perf/regressions
migration_instructions: Enable 'counterfactual-guard-v1' in eval policy to opt into PR gating. See docs/eval/counterfactual-anchor.md for config fields, allowlist usage, and rollback steps.
testing_instructions: Run pytest tests/probers and scripts/backtest/counterfactual_backtest.py against historical snapshots. To simulate a sustained regression, increase perturbation intensity in examples/anchor-configs/counterfactual-guard.yaml and run nightlies.
